Earth Untold: South Korea | Hidden Tales from the Land of the Calm Morning | Free Documentary

Earth Untold - Tohoku: https://youtu.be/Tp8OAU9psoU

The country was one of the poorest in the world at the end of the tragic war of 1953, yet South Korea has enjoyed an incredible expansion since then and now ranks as one of the major economic powers. Urban design is a striking illustration of this dynamism. Yet, behind modern Seoul lies another Korea, once known as "the Land of the Calm Morning", where Buddhist temples awake to the light of lanterns and tea plantations and rice fields ooze serenity.

Welcome to a lesser-known Korea full of natural wonders and heir to a millennium-old civilization.

snippet.title: World's Largest Isolated Tribe | Mashco Piro: Living Like 20,000 Years Ago | Free Documentary
snippet.description:
World's Largest Isolated Tribe | Mashco Piro: Living Like 20,000 Years Ago | Free Documentary

Watch 'Naga - The Tribe That Took Human Heads' here: https://youtu.be/vE-poEIRGCo

Deep in the Peruvian Amazon live the Mashco Piro, believed to be the world's largest isolated Indigenous people. Having fled the brutality of the rubber boom more than a century ago, they have remained separated from modern society ever since. But today, mysterious encounters along the river are bringing them closer to the outside world. 

As anthropologists, villagers, missionaries and criminals compete to shape their future, this documentary explores one of the most sensitive and controversial questions of our time: should an isolated people be contacted at all?

snippet.title: Holy Wars: In the Name of Christ
snippet.description:
Why did wars erupt in the name of peace? Discover how faith, violence, and the Crusades shaped history and still influence us today in this deep dive into "holy war."

Explore the complex relationship between religion and warfare, focusing on the Crusades—from their roots in medieval piety to the creation of powerful military orders like the Knights Templar. This video uncovers how calls for holy war in Christianity and Islam led to centuries of bloodshed, revealing both the religious motivations and the brutal realities of the crusader campaigns. Learn how political ambitions, economic interests, and cultural exchanges forged a dynamic, often tense, multicultural society in the Holy Land, impacting Europe, Byzantium, and the Islamic empires alike.

You'll witness the shifting alliances, betrayals, and legendary figures—such as Richard the Lionheart, Saladin, Bernard de Clairvaux, and Frederick II—who defined this era. See how the Crusades spurred technological and scientific advancements, economic booms in Italian city-states, and ongoing struggles for power between church and monarchy. Most importantly, examine the lasting legacy: Was the clash between Christianity and Islam inevitable, or did it mask deeper questions about power, faith, and humanity? This historical documentary explores answers through the lens of both European and Middle Eastern perspectives, highlighting connections, conflicts, and the enduring ideal of knighthood beyond religious boundaries.

#History #Crusades #HolyWar #MedievalHistory #ReligiousWars #EuropeanHistory #IslamicHistory #KnightsTemplar #RichardTheLionheart #Saladin

snippet.title: America's Fourth of July? Or Donald Trump's?
snippet.description:
Ten years ago, Congress created and funded a bipartisan organization, America 250, to plan and execute celebrations across the country. Those are still going on, but President Trump wanted something else. The White House, after staffing disagreements, set up Freedom 250 — a separate, public/private entity — to do things more to his liking, It seems predictable that, rather than a Fourth of July celebration for Americans of all political persuasions, he’s advertising the massive fireworks display on the National Mall as “the most spectacular TRUMP RALLY of them all, a ‘TRIBUTE TO AMERICA.’”

Abby Phillip's "NewsNight" panel debates the nature of the planned celebrations, and Kaitlan Collins goes inside the Great American State Fair on Washington's National Mall.

0:00 Did Freedom 250 commit wire fraud?
1:22 Davis: "With Trump being president, anything he does becomes political"
5:45 Egbewole "We do have a problem of feeling pessimistic about being American"
6:21 "The criticism of [the Great American State Fair] is that it's Trump-coded"
9:56 Inside Trump's State Fair

snippet.title: Metropolis: Carthage
snippet.description:
Discover the rise and fall of ancient Carthage—a powerful metropolis where trade, ambition, and legend shaped the Mediterranean world for centuries.

In this captivating historical documentary, journey back to the days when Carthage stood as the New York of the ancient world—a hub of commerce, innovation, and cultural exchange nestled on the North African coast. Follow the story of Margot, a merchant who faces danger and destiny on the open sea, and explore how Carthage grew from a Phoenician trading outpost into a thriving superpower whose influence drew people from across Europe, Africa, and beyond.

Learn how Carthaginian ingenuity fueled architectural marvels, cutting-edge metallurgy, and unmatched naval dominance. Delve into the daily lives of its citizens—merchants, artisans, slaves—and uncover secrets of Punic society, its unique approach to governance, and the rituals that both inspired awe and ignited controversy. See how Carthage’s wealth and strategic location attracted admiration and hatred—ultimately leading to one of the most tragic destructions in ancient history at the hands of Rome.

Through archaeological discoveries, expert interviews, and vivid storytelling, this video unveils the enduring legacy of Carthage, from the grandeur of its fabled port to the mysteries of child sacrifice and the resilience of its culture. Understand why the legend of Carthage has cast its spell across millennia and why its story still resonates today.

#History #Carthage #AncientCivilizations #MediterraneanHistory #Archaeology #Tunisia #Phoenicians #RomanEmpire #WorldHistory #HistoricalDocumentary

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP02
snippet.description:
Discover how factories, not just fleets, determined who won the World Wars—and how the USS Enterprise became a symbol of American might and innovation.

This video reveals the hidden engine of military victory: war production. Dive deep into why World War II was not merely a contest of naval power but a battle of factories, mass production, and industrial ingenuity. Follow the remarkable journey of the USS Enterprise, the most decorated aircraft carrier in US Navy history, from its critical role in the Pacific battles to its rapid wartime repairs—often while still under fire. Explore how the US Navy and iconic shipyards like Newport News mobilized massive workforces, including women and minorities, to outproduce Axis powers, leading to overwhelming numerical and technological advantages.

We also trace the evolution of aircraft carriers, examining pivotal moments like the battles of Midway and the Philippine Sea, and how limitations like the Washington Naval Treaty inadvertently pushed innovation forward. Japanese and US strategies, pilot training, and supply challenges are explored in detail, highlighting how logistics and shipbuilding speed played a decisive role. The story continues beyond WWII, charting the rise of the nuclear-powered USS Enterprise and the supercarrier era, up to current debates about the future of these naval giants amid rising competition from China.

If you want to understand how industry shaped history, from WWII to the Cold War and today’s global seas, this is the untold story you can’t miss.

#History #AircraftCarriers #USSEnterprise #WorldWarII #WarProduction #NavalHistory #MilitaryInnovation #EssexClass #PacificWar #NavalEngineering

snippet.title: Beeny's Restoration Nightmare: S01 EP03
snippet.description:
Sarah Beeny races against time to save her 200-year-old stately home, transforming it from crumbling ruin to wedding venue in just eight months—against all odds.

Watch as Sarah and husband Graham fight relentless dry rot, endless renovations, and last-minute disasters to turn Rise Hall—a 97-room, 30-acre Georgian mansion—into a breathtaking location ready for its very first wedding. From battling Britain's worst winter to racing for inspections, securing licences, and rushing to create opulent period bedrooms, every step is a race against looming deadlines and mounting stress. Can they pull off the transformation in time to give bride Selina and groom Ben the perfect day, and save their beloved home for future generations?

This episode chronicles all the drama, ambition, and creativity of restoring a historic property on a shoestring. See room makeovers inspired by grand country houses, behind-the-scenes chaos as wedding day approaches, and the inspiring teamwork that turns challenge after challenge into triumph. With exclusive looks at the regency, Victorian and contemporary suites, and the metamorphosis of an old sports hall into a dazzling reception space, this is a must-watch for anyone fascinated by renovations, wedding planning, or British heritage. Will Sarah and Graham secure the crucial wedding licence, complete their vision, and launch Rise Hall into a new era?

snippet.title: Black Paradise | Indonesia: Drowning in a Toxic Flood | Free Documentary
snippet.description:
Black Paradise | Indonesia: Drowning in a Toxic Flood | Free Documentary

Lamalera - Indonesia's Last Whaling Culture: https://youtu.be/E9O1XBS0Aq4

We meet Daru, an activist respected by the population and feared by the authorities. For the past 15 years, living on Bali, she has been fighting against plastic pollution, used as fuel by many factories spitting out black fumes. Microplastic particles contaminate not only the air, but also food productions. Despite a ban on plastic waste imports in 2019, thousands of tons still arrive illegally from Europe, South Korea and Canada.

Indonesia faces an irreversible ecological crisis driven by aggressive resource exploitation, replacing biodiverse forests with mines and factories. This industrialization has polluted oceans, devastated local fishing, and threatened uncontacted tribes. Paradoxically, the country is highly vulnerable to climate change, forcing the government to build a new capital in Borneo because Jakarta is sinking. However, this massive relocation project is causing further deforestation and displacing local communities.

snippet.title: The Tribe That Left the Forest | Mlabri: Asia's Forgotten People | Free Documentary
snippet.description:
The Tribe That Left the Forest | Mlabri: Asia's Forgotten Forest People | Free Documentary

World's Largest Isolated Tribe - Mashco Piro: https://youtu.be/ebfaLtXrGx4

Deep in the forests along the borders of Thailand and Laos lived one of the last hunter-gatherer peoples of Asia. For generations, the Mlabri survived beneath the dense jungle canopy, moving through the wilderness and living in simple shelters made from leaves and branches. In the early 2000s, their nomadic way of life begin to disappear, as they were resettled in villages and missions by governments and aid organizations. Today, the Mlabri stand between two worlds: the traditions of their forest-dwelling ancestors and the realities of modern life.

This documentary follows the story of a people whose ancient lifestyle survived into the 21st century. Through rare access to Mlabri communities, we explore their history, culture, and memories of a time when the rainforest was their only home. As modernization reaches even the most remote corners of Southeast Asia, the Mlabri offer a glimpse into a way of life that is rapidly vanishing from our world.

This documentary first aired in 2016

snippet.description:

See the human shield running alongside Kim Jong-un's limousine and uncover the secrets of 'The Beast'—the US President's armored car that's a mobile fortress. Learn about the historic Swiss Guard protecting the Pope and the private army that guards Vladimir Putin and his countless estates. These are tales of unimaginable luxury, absolute power, and constant danger.

snippet.title: She Fell 10,000 ft And Survived The Jungle: The Juliane Koepcke Story
snippet.description:
Juliane Koepcke was the sole survivor of LANSA Flight 508 — a plane that broke apart at 10,000 feet over the Peruvian Amazon on Christmas Eve, 1971. She survived the fall. She survived 11 days alone in the jungle with no map, no compass, and a maggot-infested wound. Other passengers survived the crash too — they died waiting for help that came too late. We spoke with jungle survival specialist Anthony Giardenelli to break down exactly what Koepcke did right, and the catastrophic negligence that made it all preventable.

snippet.title: The World's Most Terrifying Places! 5 Locations You Can Never Visit!
snippet.description:
Are there places on Earth so dangerous that entry is strictly forbidden, and the land itself is a deadly trap? In this video, we'll take you on a journey to the 5 most terrifying places in the world, which are a dark legacy of humanity.

From the contaminated zone of Chernobyl and the abandoned city of Pripyat, through the world's longest minefield in the Sahara, to the French "Red Zone," where the land has been toxic since World War I. Learn the stories of places closed due to wars, nuclear disasters, and industrial contamination, which have forever changed the face of our planet. These are tales of an unseen threat that lurks just beneath the surface.

If you are fascinated by abandoned places, dark secrets, and stories that send shivers down your spine, this video is for you.

📌 Subscribe to the channel to discover more extraordinary places with us!
